end.claim: At the Central Celtic Sea site, the modelled limitation pattern shows dissolved iron limiting the spring bloom and DIN limiting summer growth, robust to nutrient-parameter variation, so dFe should be included in shelf-sea models.

decisive_move.sentence: The time-depth inference of Felim versus Nlim from the calibrated, dFe-enabled model is what produces the seasonal co-limitation claim.

gates.evidence: No new data were acquired: all observations come from earlier UK SSB cruises (p. 4). The claim faced parameter sensitivity tests that could have moved the timing of Fe limitation (p. 11), but no rival was stated, and calibration and validation draw on the same Birchill et al. dFe data (p. 4). Parameters were tuned by trial-and-error against the data, so nothing was fixed in advance.

limits: The paper makes no explicit 'first' or 'previously unknown' statement; it credits Birchill et al. (2017) with first suggesting the co-limitation (p. 14). The same Birchill et al. dFe data are used both to calibrate (p. 4: to 'find the closest match to the vertical profiles of dFe data') and to validate the model, which the paper calls 'independent'. By inference, the validation is not independent of the calibration. Calibration was trial-and-error, with no reported objective function or skill metric. The 'hundreds of experiments' and their rejected parameter sets are not shown. Uncertainty on the limitation pattern is qualitative: there is a sensitivity spread and an inter-annual standard deviation, but no formal error. Sensitivity was one-at-a-time, with no interaction tests. The remDOM sensitivity, atmospheric Fe input, and multiple plankton functional types were not tested. The model mismatches (April dFe profiles, DIN, zooplankton in 2014, lower spring PP) are explained by auxiliaries without tests. Sub-claim at a different status: NPP is more sensitive to the benthic flux rates than to the half-saturation constants (regularity_in_range within the tested ±50% and literature ranges, p. 11). The process before submission is not visible: no review file was supplied.
